newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Sewon, Miwon fall on absorption plan.
newsitem.headline: Sewon, Miwon fall on absorption plan.

text.p: Shares in South Korea's Sewon Co and its sister firm Miwon Co went limit-down in late Thursday trading on an announcement that Sewon would absorb Miwon, brokers said.
Sewon was down 7,900 won to 91,600 and Miwon fell 1,700 won to 19,900.
Brokers said the shares fell because rumours of the merger between the two companies had circulated recently and they now had faded as a factor with the announcement.
"Investors think the absorption would hardly make any big immediate contribution to earnings of the companies," said a Hyundai Securities broker.
A statement from the Securities Supervisory Board said Sewon planned to absorb Miwon on November 1.
Brokers said Sewon was also pressured by rumours that a U.S. court had fined the company $10 million for price-fixing.
A Sewon official confirmed it was involved in a legal action, but said a ruling had not been handed down yet.
He declined to give further details on the lawsuit.
